title: PublicHealth AirPollutionClinicPanel

stats.done_summary: Successfully completed the PublicHealth AirPollutionClinicPanel analysis. Key findings: (1) PM2.5 showed a statistically significant positive association with respiratory visits after controlling for confounders (β=0.43, p=0.036); (2) A 10 μg/m³ increase in PM2.5 was associated with 4.3 additional respiratory visits (4.0% increase); (3) 25.8% of study days exceeded WHO PM2.5 guideline of 15 μg/m³; (4) Heating degree days and flu index were stronger predictors than PM2.5 alone. Deliverables: analysis code (code/analysis.py), 8 publication-quality figures (report/images/), intermediate outputs (outputs/), and comprehensive research report (report/report.md) with methodology, results, and policy implications.
